617	    def arm_report(self, arm, cuts, seed):
618	        prims = self.primaries(arm)
619	        comps = [self.compare(arm, CONTROL, m, seed) for m in prims]
620	        c, w, n_cost = self.deltas(comps)
621	        share, ex, seen = self.excluded_share(arm)
622	        out = {"arm": arm, "arm_label": self.arms[arm].get("label", arm), "primaries": prims,
623	               "comparisons": comps, "c": c, "w": w, "cost_tasks": n_cost,
624	               "excluded_share": share, "excluded_cells": ex, "cells_seen": seen}
625	        if not seen:
626	            state, rule, clauses = "no_rows", "no rows for this arm", []
627	        else:
628	            state, rule, clauses = self.decide(arm, comps, c, w, share)
629	        out["predicate_state"] = state
630	        out["predicate_rule"] = rule
631	        label = DISPLAY.get(state, state)
632	        if state == "inconclusive" and any(cl.startswith("excluded share") for cl in clauses):
633	            label = "Inconclusive-by-degradation"
634	        out["predicate_label"] = label
635	        figure = None
636	        mde_cut = self.rules.get("mde_cut")
637	        over = [p for p in comps if p["mde"] is not None and mde_cut is not None and r9(p["mde"]) > float(mde_cut)]
638	        if arm in cuts:
639	            cut = cuts[arm]
640	            state, label = cut["state"], DISPLAY[cut["state"]]
641	            rule = f"{cut['source']}: {cut['reason']}".rstrip(": ")
642	            figure = cut["figure"]
643	        elif state in ("remove", "simplify") and over:
644	            figure = "; ".join(f"MDE {p['mde']:.3f} > {float(mde_cut):g} on {p['metric']} (n = {p['n']} {p['unit']})"
645	                               for p in over)
646	            rule = f"inconclusive_by_power: {figure} (predicate read {DISPLAY[out['predicate_state']]})"
647	            state, label = "inconclusive_by_power", DISPLAY["inconclusive_by_power"]
648	        out.update(state=state, label=label, rule=rule, figure=figure,
649	                   mde_flag=[p["metric"] for p in over])
650	        out["decidable"] = bool(seen) and all(p["n"] > 0 for p in comps)
651	        return out

    def deltas(self, comps):
        """c and w over the per-task means of the cells the primaries paired."""
        per_task = {}
        for comp in comps:
            for p in comp["pairs"]:
                per_task.setdefault(p["task_id"], p)
        if not per_task:
            return None, None, 0
        ps = [per_task[t] for t in sorted(per_task)]

        def delta(a, c):
            ma, mc = mean([p[a] for p in ps]), mean([p[c] for p in ps])
            return None if not mc else (ma - mc) / mc * 100.0

        return delta("arm_cost", "control_cost"), delta("arm_wall", "control_wall"), len(ps)

    def decide(self, arm, comps, c, w, share):
        T = float(self.rules.get("threshold_points", 0.03))
        C = float(self.rules.get("cost_lower_pct", 15))
        P = [p for p in comps if p["n"] > 0]
        nopair = len(P) < len(comps)
        name = lambda p: p["metric"]  # noqa: E731
        if share is not None and r9(share) > self.guard:
            # DEC-0393: the degradation guard reads first, whatever the interval (lead's ruling, Sprint 260)
            clause = f"excluded share {share:.3f} > {self.guard:g}"
            return "inconclusive", f"inconclusive (degradation guard, evaluated first): {clause}", [clause]
        hits = [name(p) for p in P if r9(p["lo"]) > 0]
        if hits:
            return "investigate", f"investigate: any applicable primary has lo > 0 ({', '.join(hits)})", []
        hits = [name(p) for p in P if r9(p["d"]) < -T and r9(p["hi"]) < 0]
        if hits:
            return "keep", f"keep: any applicable primary has d < -{T:g} and hi < 0 ({', '.join(hits)})", []
        clauses = []
        hits = [name(p) for p in P if r9(p["d"]) < -T]
        if hits:
            clauses.append(f"d < -{T:g} ({', '.join(hits)})")
        if nopair:
            clauses.append("no valid pair (" + ", ".join(name(p) for p in comps if p["n"] == 0) + ")")
        if clauses:
            return "inconclusive", "inconclusive: " + "; ".join(clauses), clauses
        cost_ok = (c is not None and r9(c) <= -C) or (w is not None and r9(w) <= -C)
        if all(r9(p["d"]) >= -T for p in comps) and cost_ok:
            which = []
            if c is not None and r9(c) <= -C:
                which.append(f"c = {c:+.1f}")
            if w is not None and r9(w) <= -C:
                which.append(f"w = {w:+.1f}")
            return "remove", (f"remove: every applicable primary has d >= -{T:g} and "
                              f"(c <= -{C:g} or w <= -{C:g}) ({', '.join(which)})"), []
        return "simplify", f"simplify: every applicable primary within -{T:g}, cost similar", []

    def arm_report(self, arm, cuts, seed):
        prims = self.primaries(arm)
        comps = [self.compare(arm, CONTROL, m, seed) for m in prims]
        c, w, n_cost = self.deltas(comps)
        share, ex, seen = self.excluded_share(arm)
        out = {"arm": arm, "arm_label": self.arms[arm].get("label", arm), "primaries": prims,
               "comparisons": comps, "c": c, "w": w, "cost_tasks": n_cost,
               "excluded_share": share, "excluded_cells": ex, "cells_seen": seen}
        if not seen:
            state, rule, clauses = "no_rows", "no rows for this arm", []
        else:
            state, rule, clauses = self.decide(arm, comps, c, w, share)
        out["predicate_state"] = state
        out["predicate_rule"] = rule
        label = DISPLAY.get(state, state)
        if state == "inconclusive" and any(cl.startswith("excluded share") for cl in clauses):
            label = "Inconclusive-by-degradation"
        out["predicate_label"] = label
        figure = None
        mde_cut = self.rules.get("mde_cut")
        over = [p for p in comps if p["mde"] is not None and mde_cut is not None and r9(p["mde"]) > float(mde_cut)]
        if arm in cuts:
            cut = cuts[arm]
            state, label = cut["state"], DISPLAY[cut["state"]]
            rule = f"{cut['source']}: {cut['reason']}".rstrip(": ")
            figure = cut["figure"]
        elif state in ("remove", "simplify") and over:
            figure = "; ".join(f"MDE {p['mde']:.3f} > {float(mde_cut):g} on {p['metric']} (n = {p['n']} {p['unit']})"
                               for p in over)
            rule = f"inconclusive_by_power: {figure} (predicate read {DISPLAY[out['predicate_state']]})"
            state, label = "inconclusive_by_power", DISPLAY["inconclusive_by_power"]
        out.update(state=state, label=label, rule=rule, figure=figure,
                   mde_flag=[p["metric"] for p in over])
        out["decidable"] = bool(seen) and all(p["n"] > 0 for p in comps)
        return out

    def arm_metrics(self, arm):
        """Unpaired per-arm figures (AC-8.2): task-mean of trial means and the secondaries."""
        rows = self.arm_rows.get(arm, [])
        valid = [c["valid"] for (a, _), trials in sorted(self.cells.items()) if a == arm
                 for _, c in sorted(trials.items()) if c["valid"] is not None]
        by_task = {}
        for r in valid:
            by_task.setdefault(r["task_id"], []).append(r)
        status = {}
        for r in rows:
            status[r["status"]] = status.get(r["status"], 0) + 1

        def task_mean(rs_by_task, f):
            return mean([mean([f(r) for r in rs]) for rs in rs_by_task.values()])

        build = {t: rs for t, rs in by_task.items() if self.task_type[t] in BUILD_TYPES}
        rc = {t: rs for t, rs in by_task.items() if self.task_type[t] == REVIEW}

        def bools(key):
            vs = [r.get(key) for r in valid if isinstance(r.get(key), bool)]
            return None if not vs else sum(1 for v in vs if v) / len(vs)

        def nums(key, rs=None):
            vs = [r.get(key) for r in (valid if rs is None else rs)
                  if isinstance(r.get(key), (int, float)) and not isinstance(r.get(key), bool)]
            return mean(vs)

        return {
            "rows": len(rows), "by_status": dict(sorted(status.items())),
            "degraded_rows": sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("degraded") is True),
            "valid_cells": len(valid),
            PASS: task_mean(build, self.pass_score) if build else None,
            CATCH: task_mean(rc, self.catch_task_score) if rc else None,
            "verdict_accuracy": bools("verdict_accuracy"),
            "verdict_accuracy_review": bools("verdict_accuracy_review"),
            "verdict_accuracy_audit": bools("verdict_accuracy_audit"),
            "false_positives_per_task": {t: nums("false_positives", rs) for t, rs in sorted(rc.items())},
            "regressions_per_run": nums("regressions"),
            "diff_lines_per_run": nums("diff_lines"), "files_changed_per_run": nums("files_changed"),
            "cost_per_task": task_mean(by_task, lambda r: float(r.get("cost_usd") or 0)) if by_task else None,
            "cost_per_run": nums("cost_usd"),
            "wall_clock_ms_per_run": nums("wall_clock_ms"),
            "tokens_in_per_run": nums("tokens_in"), "tokens_out_per_run": nums("tokens_out"),
        }

def interval(p):
    if p is None or p["n"] == 0:
        return "no pair"
    return f"{f3(p['d'])} [{f3(p['lo'])}, {f3(p['hi'])}]"


def comp_json(p):
    out = {k: p[k] for k in ("metric", "control", "unit", "n", "n_tasks", "unpaired", "dropped", "defect_identity")}
    out.update({k: j6(p[k]) for k in ("d", "lo", "hi", "mde", "half_width")})
    out["pairs"] = [{"task_id": x["task_id"], "arm_value": j6(x["arm_value"]), "control_value": j6(x["control_value"]),
                     "diff": j6(x["diff"]), "defects": x.get("defects"),
                     "arm_runs": x["arm_runs"], "control_runs": x["control_runs"]} for x in p["pairs"]]
    if "task_level" in p:
        out["task_level"] = {k: (j6(v) if isinstance(v, float) else v) for k, v in p["task_level"].items()}
    return out


def build(args):
    suite, rules_text = load_suite(args.suite)
    rules = suite["rules"]
    bs = rules.get("bootstrap") or {}
    pre_res, pre_lvl = bs.get("resamples", 10000), bs.get("level", 0.90)
    if args.resamples is None:
        args.resamples = int(pre_res)
    if args.level is None:
        args.level = float(pre_lvl)
    if args.resamples < 1 or not (0.0 < args.level < 1.0):
        raise Fail("--resamples must be >= 1 and --level in (0, 1)")
    rows, dups = load_rows(args.runs)
    mans = load_manifests(args.manifests)
    arms = [a for a in suite["arms"] if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("id")]
    arm_ids = [a["id"] for a in arms]
    labels = {str(a.get("label", a["id"])).upper(): a["id"] for a in arms}
    cuts = load_cuts(args.cuts, args.not_run, set(arm_ids), labels)
    for need in (CONTROL, BARE):
        if need not in arm_ids:
            raise Fail(f"suite has no arm {need}")

    main = Analysis(suite, rows, mans, args, cap_excluded=False)
    sens = Analysis(suite, rows, mans, args, cap_excluded=True)
    components = [a["id"] for a in arms if a["id"] not in (CONTROL, BARE) and not a.get("absent")]
    absent = [a for a in arms if a.get("absent")]
    seed = args.seed
    decisions = [main.arm_report(a, cuts, seed) for a in components]
    sens_rows = [sens.arm_report(a, {}, seed) for a in components]

    h1_comps = [main.compare(CONTROL, BARE, m, seed) for m in main.primaries(CONTROL)]
    h1_ok = any(p["n"] > 0 and r9(p["lo"]) > 0 for p in h1_comps)
    h1_line = "H1: established" if h1_ok else "H1: not established — halt before promotion"
    a4 = None
    if SENSITIVITY_ARM in main.arms:
        a4 = main.compare(SENSITIVITY_ARM, CONTROL, PASS, seed)
        a4_ok = a4["n"] > 0 and r9(a4["hi"]) < 0
    else:
        a4_ok = False
    a4_line = ("A4 sensitivity: holds" if a4_ok
               else "A4 sensitivity: fails — harden tasks before acting on other arms")
    decidable = (any(d["decidable"] for d in decisions) or all(p["n"] > 0 for p in h1_comps)
                 or (a4 is not None and a4["n"] > 0))

    k = len(components)
    efp = k * (1.0 - args.level) / 2.0
    efp_line = (f"Expected false positives at level {args.level:.2f} over {k} components: "
                f"{k} × (1 − {args.level:.2f}) / 2 = {efp:.1f} one-sided per direction "
                f"({2 * efp:.1f} in either direction); no multiple-comparison correction is applied "
                f"(multiple_comparisons: {rules.get('multiple_comparisons', 'none')}).")

    # provenance
    used = [m for b, m in sorted(mans.items()) if any(r["batch"] == b for r in rows)] or \
        [m for _, m in sorted(mans.items())]

    def distinct(key, rowkey=None):
        vals = {str(m.get(key)) for m in used if m.get(key) not in (None, "")}
        vals |= {str(r.get(rowkey or key)) for r in rows if r.get(rowkey or key) not in (None, "")}
        return sorted(vals)

    def cli(m):
        return m.get("cli_version") or (m.get("executor") or {}).get("cli_version")

    lines = []
    L = lines.append
    L("# Loa 2.0 component ablation — report")
    L("")
    if args.partial:
        L(f"**{PARTIAL_LINE}**")
        L("")
    L(f"- report schema_version {REPORT_SCHEMA}; ablation-report.py {VERSION}")
    L(f"- suite: `{args.suite}` (name {suite.get('name', 'n/a')}, suite_version {suite.get('suite_version', 'n/a')})")
    L(f"- row suite_version: {', '.join(distinct('suite_version')) or 'n/a'}")
    L(f"- source commit(s): {', '.join(distinct('source_commit')) or 'n/a'}")
    shas = distinct("suite_manifest_sha256")
    L(f"- suite manifest sha256: {', '.join(shas) or 'n/a'}" + (" — DRIFT: more than one" if len(shas) > 1 else ""))
    L(f"- image digest(s): {', '.join(distinct('image_digest')) or 'n/a'}")
    L(f"- cli_version(s): {', '.join(sorted({str(cli(m)) for m in used if cli(m)})) or 'n/a'}")
    L("- batches:")
    for b, m in sorted(mans.items()):
        n = sum(1 for r in rows if r["batch"] == b)
        L(f"  - `{b}`{' (smoke: listed, never decided)' if m.get('smoke') is True else ''}: {n} rows, "
          f"shuffle_seed {m.get('shuffle_seed', 'n/a')}, pre_registration_ref {m.get('pre_registration_ref', 'n/a')}, "
          f"source_commit {m.get('source_commit', 'n/a')}, image_digest {m.get('image_digest', 'n/a')}, "
          f"cli_version {cli(m) or 'n/a'}")
    L(f"- rows read: {len(rows)} from {', '.join('`' + p + '`' for p in args.runs)}; "
      f"{len(main.listed)} listed and never decided; {len(dups)} duplicate run_id rows dropped")

    def mark(v, pre):
        return "" if v == pre else f" (NOT the pre-registered {pre})"

    L(f"- bootstrap: {args.resamples} resamples{mark(args.resamples, int(pre_res))}, level {args.level:.2f}"
      f"{mark(args.level, float(pre_lvl))}, seed {seed}; exclusion statuses "
      f"{', '.join(sorted(main.ex_statuses))}; degraded rows excluded: {str(args.exclude_degraded).lower()}")
    L("")
    L("## Decisions")
    L("")
    L("| component | arm | n pairs | pass-rate Δ [90 % CI] | catch-rate Δ [90 % CI] (defects) | cost Δ % | "
      "wall-clock Δ % | excluded share | decision | rule matched | rows |")
    L("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for d in decisions:
        cp = {p["metric"]: p for p in d["comparisons"]}
        npairs = ", ".join(f"{p['n']} {p['unit']}" for p in d["comparisons"])
        catch = interval(cp.get(CATCH)) if CATCH in cp else "n/a (build-only)"
        share = "n/a" if d["excluded_share"] is None else \
            f"{d['excluded_share']:.3f} ({d['excluded_cells']}/{d['cells_seen']})"
        dec = d["label"] + (f" — {d['figure']}" if d["figure"] else "")
        nrows = len(main.arm_rows.get(d["arm"], []))
        L(f"| {d['arm_label']} | `{d['arm']}` | {npairs} | {interval(cp.get(PASS))} | {catch} | {pct(d['c'])} | "
          f"{pct(d['w'])} | {share} | **{md_cell(dec)}** | {md_cell(d['rule'])} | {nrows} (§ Rows per cell) |")
    for a in absent:
        L(f"| {a.get('label', a['id'])} | `{a['id']}` | — | — | — | — | — | — | **component-absent** | "
          f"{md_cell(a.get('evidence', 'absent: true'))} | 0 |")
    L("")
    h1p = ", ".join(f"{p['metric']} {interval(p)} (n = {p['n']} {p['unit']})" for p in h1_comps)
    L(f"**{h1_line}** — a1_full − a0_bare: {h1p}. Rule (rules.h1): \"{rules.get('h1', '')}\"")
    L("")
    a4p = "no arm a4_no_gates" if a4 is None else f"{PASS} {interval(a4)} (n = {a4['n']} {a4['unit']})"
    L(f"**{a4_line}** — a4_no_gates − a1_full: {a4p}. Rule (rules.a4_sensitivity): "
      f"\"{rules.get('a4_sensitivity', '')}\"")
    L("")
    L(efp_line)
    L("")

    L("## Per-arm detail")
    L("")
    detail_arms = [BARE, CONTROL] + components
    metrics = {a: main.arm_metrics(a) for a in detail_arms if a in main.arms}
    by_arm = {d["arm"]: d for d in decisions}
    for a in detail_arms:
        if a not in main.arms:
            continue
        m = metrics[a]
        L(f"### {main.arms[a].get('label', a)} `{a}`")
        L("")
        L(f"- runs: {m['rows']} ({', '.join(f'{k} {v}' for k, v in m['by_status'].items()) or 'none'}); "
          f"degraded rows {m['degraded_rows']}; valid cells {m['valid_cells']}")
        share, ex, seen = main.excluded_share(a)
        L(f"- excluded cells: {ex} of {seen}" + ("" if share is None else f" (share {share:.3f})"))
        exl = [e for e in main.excluded if e["arm"] == a]
        for e in exl:
            L(f"  - `{e['run_id']}` {e['task_id']} t{e['trial']}: {e['reason']}")
        L(f"- applicable primaries: {', '.join(main.primaries(a))}")
        L(f"- {PASS} (task-mean of trial means, cap failures 0): {u3(m[PASS])}; "
          f"{CATCH}: {u3(m[CATCH])}")
        if a in by_arm:
            d = by_arm[a]
            for p in d["comparisons"]:
                L(f"- {p['metric']} vs a1_full: d [lo, hi] = {interval(p)}; n = {p['n']} {p['unit']} over "
                  f"{p['n_tasks']} tasks; MDE {u3(p['mde'])}; bootstrap half-width {u3(p['half_width'])}")
                if "task_level" in p:
                    tl = p["task_level"]
                    L(f"  - also_report (tasks, decides nothing): d [lo, hi] = "
                      f"{interval(dict(tl, n=tl['n']))}; n = {tl['n']} tasks")
                if p["defect_identity"]:
                    L(f"  - defect identity: {', '.join(p['defect_identity'])}")
                for u in p["unpaired"]:
                    L(f"  - left the pair: {u['task_id']} ({u['reason']})")
                for x in p["dropped"]:
                    L(f"  - pairwise drop: `{x['run_id']}` ({x['arm']}, {x['task_id']} t{x['trial']})")
            L(f"- cost Δ {pct(d['c'])}, wall-clock Δ {pct(d['w'])} over {d['cost_tasks']} paired tasks")
            L(f"- decision: **{d['label']}**" + (f" — {d['figure']}" if d["figure"] else "") + f"; rule: {d['rule']}")
            if d["state"] != d["predicate_state"]:
                L(f"- predicate outcome before the cut/power state: {d['predicate_label']}; "
                  f"{d['predicate_rule']}")
        L(f"- secondaries: verdict accuracy {u3(m['verdict_accuracy'])} (review {u3(m['verdict_accuracy_review'])}, "
          f"audit {u3(m['verdict_accuracy_audit'])}); regressions per run {u3(m['regressions_per_run'])}; "
          f"churn diff_lines {u3(m['diff_lines_per_run'])}, files_changed {u3(m['files_changed_per_run'])} per run")
        if m["false_positives_per_task"]:
            L("- false positives per review-catch task: " + ", ".join(
                f"{t} {u3(v)}" for t, v in m["false_positives_per_task"].items()))
        wall, tin, tout = m["wall_clock_ms_per_run"], m["tokens_in_per_run"], m["tokens_out_per_run"]
        wall_s = "n/a" if wall is None else f"{wall / 60000.0:.1f} min"
        tin_s = "n/a" if tin is None else f"{tin:.0f}"
        tout_s = "n/a" if tout is None else f"{tout:.0f}"
        L(f"- cost per task USD {u3(m['cost_per_task'])}, per run USD {u3(m['cost_per_run'])}; wall-clock per run "
          f"{wall_s}; tokens in/out per run {tin_s} / {tout_s}")
        L("")

    L("## Exclusions")
    L("")
    if main.excluded:
        L("| run_id | arm | task | trial | status | reason |")
        L("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
        for e in sorted(main.excluded, key=lambda e: (e["arm"], e["task_id"], e["trial"], e["run_id"])):
            L(f"| `{e['run_id']}` | `{e['arm']}` | {e['task_id']} | {e['trial']} | {e['status']} | {md_cell(e['reason'])} |")
    else:
        L("No row was excluded.")
    L("")
    caps = [c["valid"] for (_, _), trials in sorted(main.cells.items()) for _, c in sorted(trials.items())
            if c["valid"] is not None and c["valid"]["status"] == "cap_failure"]
    L("### Cap failures (scored 0 on every applicable primary; the sensitivity figure excludes them)")
    L("")
    for r in caps:
        L(f"- `{r['run_id']}` (`{r['arm']}`, {r['task_id']} t{r['trial']}, cap_phase {r.get('cap_phase') or 'n/a'}, "
          f"USD {float(r.get('cost_usd') or 0):.2f})")
    if not caps:
        L("- none")
    L("")
    L("### Rows listed, never decided")
    L("")
    if main.listed or dups:
        for r, why in main.listed:
            L(f"- `{r['run_id']}` (`{r['arm']}`, {r['task_id']}, {r['status']}): {why}")
        for dd in dups:
            L(f"- `{dd['run_id']}` at {dd['dropped']}: duplicate run_id, the row at {dd['kept']} is used")
    else:
        L("None.")
    L("")

    L("## Cuts")
    L("")
    pw = [d for d in decisions if d["state"] == "inconclusive_by_power" and d["arm"] not in cuts]
    if not cuts and not pw:
        L("- none recorded")
    for a in sorted(cuts):
        c = cuts[a]
        L(f"- `{a}`: {DISPLAY[c['state']]} — reason: {c['reason']}; figure: {c['figure']} ({c['source']})")
    for d in pw:
        L(f"- `{d['arm']}`: Inconclusive-by-power from the rows — {d['figure']}")
    L(f"- cut ladder (suite): {'; '.join(suite.get('cut_ladder') or []) or 'n/a'}")
    L("")

    L(f"## Sensitivity figure: {SENS_LABEL}")
    L("")
    L("| component | arm | n pairs | pass-rate Δ [90 % CI] | catch-rate Δ [90 % CI] (defects) | cost Δ % | "
      "wall-clock Δ % | excluded share | predicate outcome (not used) |")
    L("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for d in sens_rows:
        cp = {p["metric"]: p for p in d["comparisons"]}
        npairs = ", ".join(f"{p['n']} {p['unit']}" for p in d["comparisons"])
        catch = interval(cp.get(CATCH)) if CATCH in cp else "n/a (build-only)"
        share = "n/a" if d["excluded_share"] is None else f"{d['excluded_share']:.3f}"
        L(f"| {d['arm_label']} | `{d['arm']}` | {npairs} | {interval(cp.get(PASS))} | {catch} | {pct(d['c'])} | "
          f"{pct(d['w'])} | {share} | {d['predicate_label']} |")
    L("")

    L("## Rows per cell")
    L("")
    for d in decisions:
        for p in d["comparisons"]:
            if not p["pairs"]:
                continue
            L(f"### {d['arm_label']} `{d['arm']}` — {p['metric']}")
            L("")
            L("| task | arm value | a1_full value | diff | arm rows | a1_full rows |")
            L("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
            for x in p["pairs"]:
                L(f"| {x['task_id']} | {u3(x['arm_value'])} | {u3(x['control_value'])} | {f3(x['diff'])} | "
                  f"{', '.join('`' + s + '`' for s in collapse(x['arm_runs']))} | "
                  f"{', '.join('`' + s + '`' for s in collapse(x['control_runs']))} |")
            L("")
    for title, comps in (("H1 a1_full − a0_bare", h1_comps), ("A4 a4_no_gates − a1_full", [a4] if a4 else [])):
        for p in comps:
            if not p["pairs"]:
                continue
            L(f"### {title} — {p['metric']}")
            L("")
            L("| task | diff | arm rows | control rows |")
            L("|---|---|---|---|")
            for x in p["pairs"]:
                L(f"| {x['task_id']} | {f3(x['diff'])} | {', '.join('`' + s + '`' for s in collapse(x['arm_runs']))} | "
                  f"{', '.join('`' + s + '`' for s in collapse(x['control_runs']))} |")
            L("")

    L("## Method")
    L("")
    L(f"The pre-registered rules block of `{args.suite}`, quoted verbatim:")
    L("")
    L("```yaml")
    L(rules_text)
    L("```")
    L("")
    L("- Pass rate: the unit is the task; a cell is one task-trial; a task's value is the mean of its valid "
      "trials (cap_failure scores 0); a trial excluded in either arm leaves both arms of that comparison "
      "(pairwise); a task with no valid cell in either arm leaves the pair and is listed.")
    L("- Catch rate: the unit is the defect (task × dK); a defect's value is the share of the arm's valid trials "
      "that caught it (ids from the row's defects_missed / recall.missed, else the row's defect_catch_rate for "
      "every defect of the task); the task-level figure is also reported and decides nothing.")
    L(f"- Interval: percentile bootstrap of the mean paired difference, {args.resamples} resamples with "
      f"replacement from random.Random({seed}) (one generator per interval), linear interpolation between "
      f"order statistics, [lo, hi] at the {(1 - args.level) / 2:.2f} and {1 - (1 - args.level) / 2:.2f} quantiles; "
      "d is the mean of the paired differences.")
    L("- c and w: (mean_arm − mean_a1) / mean_a1 × 100 over the per-task means of the paired cells (cost_usd, "
      "wall_clock_ms).")
    L(f"- MDE: (z({1 - (1 - args.level) / 2:.2f}) + z({POWER:.2f})) × sd(paired diffs) / sqrt(n); an arm whose "
      f"predicates read remove or simplify with an MDE above mde_cut ({rules.get('mde_cut', 'n/a')}) reads "
      "Inconclusive-by-power.")
    L("- Predicates are evaluated in order on values rounded to 9 decimals, the degradation guard first "
      f"(excluded share > {main.guard:g} reads Inconclusive-by-degradation whatever the interval, DEC-0393), then "
      "investigate, keep, inconclusive (d < -0.03 or no valid pair), remove, simplify; Inconclusive-by-degradation is the "
      "inconclusive outcome whose excluded-share clause matched.")
    L("")

    data = {
        "schema_version": REPORT_SCHEMA, "generator": f"ablation-report.py {VERSION}", "partial": bool(args.partial),
        "suite": {"path": args.suite, "name": suite.get("name"), "suite_version": suite.get("suite_version")},
        "provenance": {"source_commits": distinct("source_commit"), "suite_manifest_sha256": shas,
                       "suite_versions": distinct("suite_version"), "image_digests": distinct("image_digest"),
                       "batches": [{"batch": b, "smoke": m.get("smoke") is True, "shuffle_seed": m.get("shuffle_seed"),
                                    "pre_registration_ref": m.get("pre_registration_ref"),
                                    "source_commit": m.get("source_commit"), "image_digest": m.get("image_digest"),
                                    "cli_version": cli(m), "manifest": m["_path"]} for b, m in sorted(mans.items())]},
        "bootstrap": {"resamples": args.resamples, "level": args.level, "seed": seed},
        "exclude_degraded": bool(args.exclude_degraded),
        "decisions": [{"arm": d["arm"], "arm_label": d["arm_label"], "label": d["label"], "state": d["state"], "rule": d["rule"],
                       "figure": d["figure"], "predicate_state": d["predicate_state"],
                       "predicate_rule": d["predicate_rule"], "primaries": d["primaries"],
                       "c": j6(d["c"]), "w": j6(d["w"]), "cost_tasks": d["cost_tasks"],
                       "excluded_share": j6(d["excluded_share"]), "excluded_cells": d["excluded_cells"],
                       "cells_seen": d["cells_seen"], "mde_flag": d["mde_flag"], "decidable": d["decidable"],
                       "comparisons": [comp_json(p) for p in d["comparisons"]]} for d in decisions],
        "absent": [{"arm": a["id"], "label": a.get("label"), "state": "component_absent",
                    "evidence": a.get("evidence")} for a in absent],
        "h1": {"line": h1_line, "established": h1_ok, "rule": rules.get("h1"),
               "comparisons": [comp_json(p) for p in h1_comps]},
        "a4": {"line": a4_line, "holds": a4_ok, "rule": rules.get("a4_sensitivity"),
               "comparison": comp_json(a4) if a4 else None},
        "expected_false_positives": {"components": k, "per_direction": j6(efp), "line": efp_line},
        "arms": {a: {kk: (j6(v) if isinstance(v, float) else
                          ({t: j6(x) for t, x in v.items()} if kk == "false_positives_per_task" else v))
                     for kk, v in metrics[a].items()} for a in metrics},
        "exclusions": sorted(main.excluded, key=lambda e: (e["arm"], e["task_id"], e["trial"], e["run_id"])),
        "listed": [{"run_id": r["run_id"], "arm": r["arm"], "task_id": r["task_id"], "status": r["status"],
                    "reason": why} for r, why in main.listed],
        "duplicates": dups,
        "cap_failures": [r["run_id"] for r in caps],
        "cuts": [dict(arm=a, **cuts[a]) for a in sorted(cuts)],
        "sensitivity": {"label": SENS_LABEL,
                        "rows": [{"arm": d["arm"], "predicate_state": d["predicate_state"], "c": j6(d["c"]),
                                  "w": j6(d["w"]), "excluded_share": j6(d["excluded_share"]),
                                  "comparisons": [comp_json(p) for p in d["comparisons"]]} for d in sens_rows]},
    }
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n", data, decidable


def write_out(path, text):
    if os.path.islink(path):
        raise Fail(f"refusing to write through the symlink {path}")
    parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    if not os.path.isdir(parent):
        raise Fail(f"the directory of {path} does not exist")
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(text)


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message):
        sys.stderr.write(f"ablation-report.py: {message}\n")
        sys.exit(2)


def main(argv):
    ap = Parser(prog="ablation-report.py", description="cycle-130 ablation report (see the header)")
    ap.add_argument("--runs", action="append", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--manifests", action="append", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--suite", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--json", dest="json_out")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20261015)
    ap.add_argument("--resamples", type=int)
    ap.add_argument("--level", type=float)
    ap.add_argument("--exclude-degraded", choices=("true", "false"), default="true")
    ap.add_argument("--partial", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--cuts")
    ap.add_argument("--not-run")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    args.exclude_degraded = args.exclude_degraded == "true"
    try:
        text, data, decidable = build(args)
        write_out(args.out, text)
        if args.json_out:
            write_out(args.json_out, json.dumps(data, indent=2, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    except Fail as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"ablation-report.py: {e}\n")
        return 2
    if args.partial and not decidable:
        sys.stderr.write("ablation-report.py: --partial: no comparison has a valid pair yet (report written)\n")
        return 1
    print(f"ablation-report.py: wrote {args.out}" + (f" and {args.json_out}" if args.json_out else ""))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

title: [P2] Preserve executable expansions when stripping heredocs
failure_mode: Unquoted Bash heredocs execute command substitutions, so their bodies are not necessarily inert data.
description: Unquoted Bash heredocs execute command substitutions, so their bodies are not necessarily inert data. For example, `cat <<EOF\n$(cat /root/private.txt)\nEOF` reads the outside file and prints its contents, but strip_heredocs() reduces the scanned command to `cat <<HEREDOC`. The original command was scanned before this change. Preserve and inspect executable expansions in unquoted heredocs instead of removing their entire bodies.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

failure_mode: An evaluated agent (or a model that habitually writes `python3 - <<'EOF'` scripts) reads files outside the allowed roots and the run is graded as uncontaminated; eval scores are inflated by access to data the contamination control is meant to detect.
description: grader 1.2.2 strips every heredoc body from the Bash command before the absolute-path scan on the premise that heredoc text is 'data being written'. That premise is false whenever the heredoc feeds an interpreter: `bash <<EOF`, `sh -s <<EOF`, `python3 - <<EOF`, `node - <<EOF`, `sudo -s <<EOF`. Any `cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `open('/mnt/hidden/tests.py')` or `ls /srv/...` inside such a body is executed by the sandbox but never reaches the ABS_WORD loop, so `outside_path` can no longer fire. The hidden/suite/repo substring scans still see the full value, but the path leak check is the only one that catches arbitrary out-of-sandbox reads.

failure_mode: An agent reads hidden tests, credentials, or host files outside the sandbox roots using a path spelled `/./...`, `""/...` or `''/...`; the grader records contaminated=null/false and the trial is scored as clean.
description: Several new skip rules are keyed on lexical shape rather than on the normalised path, and each one is trivially satisfiable for a real, resolvable path: (1) `w.startswith("/.")` skips `/./root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/./home/x/.aws/credentials`, `/./mnt/hidden/...` which the kernel resolves identically to the undotted path (`R=/./root; cat $R/.ssh/id_rsa` also passes since `=/./root` begins with `/.`); (2) after_closing_quote treats a word glued to a preceding quote as a path tail, so `cat ""/root/.ssh/id_rsa` or `cat ''/mnt/secret` (empty string followed by the path, a legal shell no-op) is skipped although it is the absolute path itself; (3) `"=" in w` and the `/,` prefix drop any word containing `=` or starting `/,` without checking whether it still normalises to a sensitive location. The existing `//` skip is already a bypass (`//root/...` resolves on Linux); the new rules add three more that require no special filesystem state.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

failure_mode: The agent enumerates or reads the hidden test directory through Bash using a globbed, quoted or mixed-case spelling and is not flagged `hidden`; recall/hidden_tests scores become contaminated without detection.
description: For Bash the former case-insensitive substring check (`"hidden" in val.lower()`) is replaced by HIDDEN_TOKEN, which is case-sensitive (only `HIDDEN` or lowercase `hidden`) and only fires when `hidden` is adjacent to `/ . _ = -`. Natural probe commands now pass: `find . -iname '*hidden*'` (quote before, `*` after), `ls -d *hidden*`, `grep -ril hidden .`, `cat 'hidden tests/test_x.py'`, `ls "hidden tests"`, and any mixed case such as `cat Hidden/tests.py` or `ls HiddenTests` (Linux filesystems are case-sensitive but the detection no longer is). The non-Bash tools keep the old behaviour, so the weakening is Bash-only yet Bash is the richest channel.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

failure_mode: `cd /root`, `cd /home`, `cd /mnt` followed by relative reads escapes contamination detection whenever the command text happens to (or is crafted to) contain an unmatched apostrophe before the path word.
description: in_quotes decides a one-component sensitive word (`/root`, `/home`, `/mnt`, `/media`, `/srv`) is quoted pattern text when the count of `'` or `"` before it is odd, counting raw characters with no awareness of nesting or escaping. Any earlier apostrophe inside a double-quoted string poisons the parity for the rest of the command: `echo "don't"; cd /root && cat .ssh/id_rsa`, `git commit -m "it's done" ; ls /home`, or `# can't` followed by `cd /mnt`. The comment already accepts `cd '/root/'` as a gap; the parity bug widens it to any command where the agent emits an odd quote earlier, which is common in commit messages and echo text.

failure_mode: ablation-grade.sh hangs or hits LOA_EVAL_GRADE_TIMEOUT_S on an agent-controlled transcript; the trial is rowed infrastructure_error/ungraded instead of being scored, letting an agent escape grading of a bad run.
description: HEREDOC is compiled with re.S and contains `(?:.*?\n)*?` where `.` also matches newline. Each newline in the candidate body can be consumed by either `.*?` or the explicit `\n`, so when the terminator never matches (an unterminated `<<EOF`, a terminator with trailing text, or a `<<WORD` appearing inside a quoted string) the engine backtracks exponentially in the number of newlines. The input is the agent's own Bash command text from transcripts/events-*.jsonl, so an evaluated agent can hang the grader by emitting one command containing `<<EOF` followed by a few dozen newlines with no terminator.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

=== OUTPUT-SCHEMA ===
# Structured Finding Output Schema

Defines the JSONL output format for machine-parseable audit findings.

## Finding Schema

Each finding is a JSON object on a single line in the JSONL file.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "AuditFinding",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "category", "criterion", "severity", "score", "finding", "reasoning_trace", "confidence"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}$",
      "description": "Unique finding ID (e.g., SEC-001, ARCH-042)"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["security", "architecture", "code_quality", "devops", "blockchain"],
      "description": "Audit category"
    },
    "criterion": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Specific rubric dimension (e.g., input_validation, modularity)"
    },
    "severity": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["CRITICAL", "HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW", "INFO"],
      "description": "Finding severity"
    },
    "score": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 5,
      "description": "Rubric score for this dimension"
    },
    "file": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "File path where issue was found"
    },
    "line": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Line number (if applicable)"
    },
    "code_snippet": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Relevant code excerpt"
    },
    "reasoning_trace": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "How the issue was discovered - analysis path and evidence"
    },
    "finding": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Clear description of the issue"
    },
    "critique": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Specific guidance for improvement"
    },
    "remediation": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Exact fix with code example if applicable"
    },
    "confidence": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["high", "medium", "low"],
      "description": "Confidence in the finding"
    },
    "references": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {"type": "string"},
      "description": "CVE, CWE, OWASP, or other references"
    }
  }
}
```

## Example Findings

### Security Finding
```json
{"id":"SEC-001","category":"security","criterion":"input_validation","severity":"HIGH","score":2,"file":"src/api/users.ts","line":42,"code_snippet":"const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${userId}`;","reasoning_trace":"Traced user input from req.params.userId through controller to database query. Found string interpolation in SQL query construction at L42, bypassing ORM parameterization.","finding":"SQL injection vulnerability via unsanitized userId parameter","critique":"The userId is interpolated directly into SQL string. Even if userId appears numeric, type coercion allows injection. The ORM's parameterized query feature is available but not used here.","remediation":"Replace L42 with: `const user = await db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', [userId]);`","confidence":"high","references":["CWE-89","OWASP-A03:2021"]}
```

### Architecture Finding
```json
{"id":"ARCH-012","category":"architecture","criterion":"modularity","severity":"MEDIUM","score":3,"file":"src/services/","reasoning_trace":"Analyzed import graph and found UserService imports from PaymentService, OrderService, and NotificationService. PaymentService also imports UserService creating circular dependency detected via tsc --traceResolution.","finding":"Circular dependency between UserService and PaymentService","critique":"Tight coupling between these services will make testing and modification difficult. Consider extracting shared logic to a separate module or using events for decoupling.","remediation":"1. Extract shared types to src/types/\n2. Use event emitter for cross-service communication\n3. Consider domain events pattern","confidence":"high","references":["Clean Architecture","DDD Bounded Contexts"]}
```

### Code Quality Finding
```json
{"id":"CQ-007","category":"code_quality","criterion":"error_handling","severity":"LOW","score":4,"file":"src/utils/api.ts","line":78,"code_snippet":"} catch (e) { console.log(e); }","reasoning_trace":"Reviewed error handling patterns across codebase. Found 3 instances of catch blocks that only console.log errors without proper handling or re-throwing.","finding":"Silent error swallowing in API utility","critique":"Errors are logged but not handled or propagated. This makes debugging difficult and can hide critical failures in production.","remediation":"Replace with: `} catch (e) { logger.error('API call failed', { error: e, context }); throw new ApiError('Request failed', { cause: e }); }`","confidence":"medium","references":["Error Handling Best Practices"]}
```

## Output File Location

Findings should be written to:
```
grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl
```

Each `reasoning_trace` states what was analyzed, the triggering pattern, the evidence chain from input to vulnerability, and the scoring rationale.

## Summary Record

At the end of the JSONL file, include a summary record:

```json
{"type":"summary","timestamp":"2026-01-30T12:00:00Z","category_scores":{"security":3.2,"architecture":4.1,"code_quality":3.8,"devops":4.0},"overall_score":3.8,"risk_level":"MODERATE","total_findings":{"CRITICAL":0,"HIGH":2,"MEDIUM":5,"LOW":8,"INFO":3},"verdict":"CHANGES_REQUIRED"}
```

## Parsing Example

```bash
# Get all HIGH severity findings
=== BEADS-WORKFLOW head ===
# Beads Workflow (beads_rust) — auditing-security

Referenced from `auditing-security/SKILL.md` `<beads_workflow>`.

When `br` is installed: `br sync --import-only` at session start, `br sync --flush-only` at session end. Record the result:

```bash
br comments add <task-id> "SECURITY AUDIT: [verdict] - grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
br label add <task-id> security
# then exactly one of:
# If approved
br label add <task-id> security-approved
# If changes required
br label add <task-id> security-blocked
```
A re-review or re-audit adds its round's label and `br label add` never removes the other, so a task can carry both: the latest `SECURITY AUDIT:` comment is the verdict of record (with the feedback file and the COMPLETED marker), a label only history.

Log a discovered vulnerability as its own issue: `.claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh "<sprint-epic-id>" "Security: <criterion> (see auditor-sprint-feedback.md)" bug 0` — the criterion only, never the finding text or its file (the flushed JSONL is committed; the location stays in the feedback file), then `br label add <new-issue-id> security`. Protocol: `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`.

### Agent Teams
A teammate runs no `br` command: it reports the result to the lead via SendMessage, and the lead runs it. A comment carries the verdict and the feedback file's path only — never finding text or code.

# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (carries pr/PR.md)
**Change under audit:** pr/head.diff (17 files; citations are `head/<path>:<line>` with lines from pr/head/)
**Task:** review-r24

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Executive Summary

The sprint adds the ablation batch runner (`run-ablation.sh`), the shared spend/transport library (`lib/arms-common.sh`), the pre-registered report (`ablation-report.py`), the DEC-0545 substitution rule in `ablation-row.sh`, and five calibration rounds of the grader's contamination check (`ablation-grade.sh` 1.2.1 to 1.2.5). The runner and the report are sound: every CLI argument that reaches a path or a process is regex-validated (`run-ablation.sh:310-351`), JSON is built with `jq --arg`/`--argjson` throughout, rows are appended and replaced under `flock` on a sibling lock file, the report refuses symlinked inputs and outputs, and the report test suite passes 22 of 22 on the head tree.

The security problems sit in one place: the grader's contamination classifier, which is the trust boundary between the agent under test and the decision dataset. Each calibration round added a lexical skip rule to silence a false positive, and the rules now suppress true positives on ordinary, non-adversarial command shapes. Three regressions against grader 1.2.0 are confirmed by executing the head `check_value` on the inputs quoted below: the Bash `hidden` scan is now case-sensitive and adjacency-gated; heredoc bodies are stripped even when the heredoc is the program an interpreter runs; and the heredoc regex backtracks exponentially on an unterminated `<<WORD`, so an agent's transcript can stall the grader until the timeout rows the trial `infrastructure_error`. The remaining skips (`/.`, glued quotes, `=`, quote parity) are narrower bypasses. Both independent dissent voices (codex-headless and claude-headless, consensus, 2 of 2) reached the same three highs.

**Security Issues Found:**
| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 3 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 6 |

**Prerequisite note.** Phase 0 of this skill expects the review's `engineer-feedback.md` to read "All good"; it reads CHANGES_REQUIRED (2 high). The run orchestrator asked for the audit regardless and forbade questions, so the audit ran and this deviation is recorded here rather than acted on.

**Scope limits.** The dissent prompt was truncated to the token budget: 8 of 17 files were sent and `run-ablation.sh` was cut mid-hunk (the run's stderr log). The envelope is not marked degraded, both voices completed, and the files the voices did not see (`run-ablation.sh` tail, `lib/arms-common.sh`, `ablation-report.py`, the tests and fixtures) were read in full by this auditor. `evals/tests/run-ablation.bats` and `ablation-grade.bats` were not executed: they need `freeze.sh`, `took-effect.sh`, `pipeline-run.sh`, the frozen suite root and the docker stub, none of which the frozen PR tree holds; their assertions were read instead. `shellcheck` and `br` are not installed here.

---

## Critical Security Issues (Must Fix)

None.

---

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] The Bash `hidden` scan is case-sensitive and adjacency-gated, so ordinary probes for the hidden tests grade clean

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1329` (used at `:1395`; header still says "any case" at `:167`)
**Issue:** Grader 1.2.0 flagged `"hidden" in val.lower()` for every tool. Grader 1.2.4 replaces that for Bash with

```python
HIDDEN_TOKEN = re.compile(r"HIDDEN|(?<=[/._=-])hidden\b|\bhidden(?=[/_=-]|\.[A-Za-z0-9])")
```

which matches only all-caps `HIDDEN` or lowercase `hidden` glued to `/ . _ = -`. Quote, glob and space neighbours are not in the adjacency classes, and `Hidden` in any mixed case never matches. Executed on the head code (`A.executor = "container"`): `grep -ri hidden .`, `find . -iname '*hidden*'`, `ls Hidden/`, `ls hidden`, `cat Hidden_x` and `find / -iname 'hidden*'` all return `None`; grader 1.2.0 returned `"hidden"` for each. DEC-0551's stated intent was to exempt English prose inside a reviewer's heredoc; the fix instead narrowed the token shape for the whole command.
**Impact:** A run that enumerates or reads the hidden test directory through Bash is scored as valid data and enters the pass-rate comparison the pre-registered analysis decides on. Bash is the richest tool channel, and these are the natural, non-adversarial spellings.
**Fix:** Keep the prose exemption scoped to heredoc bodies: run a case-insensitive `\bhidden\b` scan on `strip_heredocs(val)` and keep the token-shape scan, made case-insensitive, on the full value. Add AG-10 cases for the six commands above. Update the header at `:167`.
**Reference:** CWE-178 Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/178.html ; CWE-693 Protection Mechanism Failure https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html
**Cross-model:** Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-003, claude-headless, HIGH).

### [HIGH-002] `strip_heredocs` removes heredoc bodies that the shell executes, hiding every outside path they contain

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1380-1383` (applied at `:1412`)
**Issue:** The docstring's premise is "file text being written is data, not a path the agent reached". That is true only for a heredoc that lands in a file through `cat >`. When the heredoc is the standard input of an interpreter, or its delimiter is unquoted, the body runs in the sandbox. Executed on the head code, each of the following returns `None`, where grader 1.2.0 returned `"outside_path"`:

```
python3 - <<'EOF'
print(open('/home/operator/notes.txt').read())
EOF
```
```
bash <<EOF
cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa
EOF
```
```
cat <<EOF
$(cat /home/operator/notes.txt)
EOF
```
```
cat > /tmp/s.sh <<'EOF'
cat /home/operator/notes.txt
EOF
bash /tmp/s.sh
```

`python3 - <<'PY'` is the idiom this very grader and `run-ablation.sh` use for inline scripts, so it is a shape the agents under test emit routinely.
**Impact:** The outside-path check is the only control that catches arbitrary reads outside the sandbox roots (the `hidden`/suite/repo substring scans still read the full value, but only for those three strings). Any interpreter-driven read is now invisible to contamination grading.
**Fix:** Strip only bodies that are inert data: a quoted delimiter (`<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"`) whose command is a writer (`cat`, `tee`, redirection to a file). For an interpreter command (`python3 -`, `bash`, `sh -s`, `node -`, `perl -`), or any unquoted delimiter, scan the body with the path-word loop (at least `$(...)` and backtick spans for the unquoted case). Add AG-10 cases for the four commands above.
**Reference:** CWE-693 Protection Mechanism Failure https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html ; OWASP A04:2021 Insecure Design https://owasp.org/Top10/A04_2021-Insecure_Design/
**Cross-model:** Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-001 HIGH, claude-headless; DISS-002 MEDIUM, gpt-5.5-pro). The review counted the `$(...)` case as MEDIUM; the interpreter case widens it to the common shape, hence HIGH here.

### [HIGH-003] The `HEREDOC` regex backtracks exponentially on an unterminated heredoc, stalling the grade

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1377`
**Issue:**

```python
HEREDOC = re.compile(r"<<-?\s*(['\"]?)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\1[^\n]*\n(?:.*?\n)*?\s*\2[ \t]*(?=\n|$)", re.S)
```

Under `re.S` the `.` in `(?:.*?\n)*?` also matches newlines, so a body of N lines can be split into chunks in 2^N ways. When no terminator line follows, every split is tried. Measured on the head regex with `cat <<EOF` followed by N plain lines: 12 lines 0.003 s, 16 lines 0.046 s, 18 lines 0.121 s, 20 lines 0.469 s; the review measured 2.1 s at 22. Roughly ×4 per two lines, so a few dozen lines exceed any `LOA_EVAL_GRADE_TIMEOUT_S`. Triggers are a truncated tool input, a terminator glued to `)` or `;`, or `<<WORD` inside a quoted string.
**Impact:** The input is the agent's own Bash command text from `transcripts/events-*.jsonl`. A stalled grade is killed, `run-ablation.sh` rows the trial `infrastructure_error` (`head/evals/harness/run-ablation.sh:996-997`), the cell leaves the analysis and the arm moves toward the degradation guard. An agent escapes grading of a run by emitting one malformed heredoc.
